column1: # Audit of the 2024 blobtools read filter.
# QUESTION: the 2024 pipeline assembled each sample's whole metagenome with
# hifiasm, used blobtools to discard non-Hamiltonella contigs, then kept only
# reads that aligned to what survived. Everything downstream inherits that
# decision, and it had never been tested. Did it discard real Hamiltonella or
# APSE sequence?
# METHOD: for all 14 samples, every contig present in the pre-filter assembly
# but absent from the filtered one was aligned against Hamiltonella defensa 5AT
# (GCA_000021705.1) and against the v2 APSE references. Any dropped contig with
# substantial, high-identity similarity is a candidate false positive. Each
# candidate was then tested for whether its sequence survives elsewhere in the
# retained assembly.
# CALIBRATION: our own retained chromosomes align to 5AT at 91.1-94.6 % weighted
# identity over 1.5-2.0 Mb. Anything below ~91 % is therefore not Hamiltonella.
# RESULT: 68,863 contigs were examined across the panel. At a threshold of >=1 kb
# aligned at >=88 % identity, 13 dropped contigs were flagged. Two of them carry
# genuine Hamiltonella or APSE sequence -- and both are fully present in the
# retained assembly, so nothing was lost. The other eleven are large contigs
# (50-647 kb) in which only 1.5-2.5 kb aligns, at 88.3-89.8 %, below the genuine
# range: a short conserved element inside aphid or other contigs.
# CONCLUSION: the blobtools filter did not remove Hamiltonella or APSE sequence.
# The read-level stage of the audit was therefore not required.
